sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Studies show that all north ______ languages except Urdu originated from the ______.
Give reasons in short phrases: Why do the scripts of Hindi, Gujarati and Punjabi bear similarities? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: All three originated from the old Brahmi script; they changed slowly over a long period from the same source.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Why is Chandrabhan of Shah Jahan's days famous? (b) Why is Badayuni famous?
questions.answer: (a) He was a Persian prose and history writer. (b) He was a historian and writer in Akbar's time.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Why did the reformers use novels, dramas, short stories and poetry? (b) Why did they use Indian languages?
questions.answer: (a) To reach the common people and stir national and social awakening. (b) To make their message understood by the masses.

questions.q: Answer in two short phrases: Give any two reasons why Hindi continued to grow though Persian and Urdu enjoyed royal patronage.
questions.answer: The Bhakti saints and poets (Tulsidas, Surdas, Kabir) used it, and it was the language of the common people.

questions.q: Answer in two short phrases: How did Kashmir lag behind in producing good literature?
questions.answer: Poverty, economic backwardness, hardly any schools or education, and the Dogra rulers' preference for Dogri.

questions.q: Answer in two short phrases: What was the role of Christian missionaries in the growth of Indian languages?
questions.answer: They published dictionaries and grammars and set up printing presses and schools that taught local languages.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: How did Punjabi love stories contribute to the growth of the Punjabi language?
questions.answer: Stories like Heer–Ranjha, Sohni–Mahiwal and Sassi–Punnu gave Punjabi its early themes and were sung for centuries.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Tulsidas used the ______ dialect. (b) Surdas used the ______ dialect.
Mark true or false: (a) Prithviraj Raso is considered the first Hindi book. (b) Tulsidas described Rama as a human being.
Fill in the blanks: (a) Urdu was called ______ in the Deccan. (b) ______ wrote Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
Answer in a word: (a) Which work of Tagore won him the Nobel Prize? (b) Who wrote Rajatarangini?
Mark true or false: (a) Urdu was written in the Persian script. (b) Gurmukhi script was widely used for all Punjabi literature even before the 19th century.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – it was mostly limited to the Adi Granth until the end of the 19th century.

questions.q: Match two items (rest are distracters): Narsi Mehta – Gujarati; Tukaram – Marathi; Lal Ded – Bengali; Waris Shah – Sindhi. Give two correct pairs.
Fill in the blanks: (a) ______ Despatch of 1854 led to universities. (b) The three universities of Calcutta, Madras and Bombay were established in ______.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: 'The Persian language was developed during the medieval period.' Support the statement with two points.
questions.answer: Persian was the court language for many centuries; Akbar had Sanskrit books and the Mahabharata translated into Persian; histories (Akbarnama, Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, Badshahnama), poetry (Amir Khusrau, Faizi) and administrative manuals were written in it.

questions.q: Mention the dialects used by Tulsidas and Surdas.
questions.answer: Tulsidas used Avadhi in the Ramcharitmanas and Surdas used Braj Bhasha in the Sur Sagar.

questions.q: How did Dinanath Nadim contribute to Kashmiri literature?
questions.answer: He was among the poets who wrote devotional and modern poetry in Kashmiri, enriching its literature.

questions.q: Who was Lal Ded?
questions.answer: A Shaivite mystic of the 14th century, probably the first to sing in the Kashmiri language.

questions.q: What was the role of the Christian missionaries in the growth of Indian languages?
questions.answer: They published the earliest dictionaries and grammars, introduced lithographic printing presses and established schools and colleges that taught local languages, producing an educated reading class.

questions.q: Name two works of Abul Fazl and one of Abdul Hamid Lahori.
questions.answer: Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari by Abul Fazl; Badshah Nama by Lahori.

questions.q: Why is Waris Shah famous in Punjabi literature?
questions.answer: His 'Heer' is the most popular early Punjabi work, a landmark in Punjabi poetry.

questions.q: Name two Hindi poets of the Bhakti period and their works.
questions.answer: Tulsidas – Ramcharit Manas; Surdas – Sur Sagar; Bihari – Satsai; Mirabai – devotional songs (any two).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Briefly describe the development of Hindi language.
questions.answer: Hindi evolved from Apabhramsha between the 7th–8th and the 14th century (Veergatha Kala), with Prithviraj Raso as the first book. Under the Bhakti movement it became devotional – Kabir, Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai. Khadi Boli, used by Khusrau, came into extensive literary use in the 19th century with Bharatendu Harishchandra, Dayanand, Premchand, Nirala and Mahadevi Verma.

questions.q: What is the role of the Persian language in medieval India?
questions.answer: Persian was the court language, so histories, administrative manuals, letters (insha) and poetry were written in it; Mughal rulers patronised it and had Sanskrit works translated; Amir Khusrau, Faizi, Abul Fazl and Chandra Bhan wrote in it.

questions.q: Write a note on Punjabi literature before the 19th century.
questions.answer: Guru Nanak was the first Punjabi poet; Sufi poets like Farid and later Bulleh Shah (kafis) and Waris Shah (Heer) wrote; Adi Granth contains poetry of the gurus; love stories of Heer–Ranjha, Sohni–Mahiwal and Sassi–Punnu gave themes; Gurmukhi was mostly confined to the Adi Granth.

questions.q: Explain the role of Bhakti poets in the growth of regional languages.
questions.answer: Poets like Tulsidas, Surdas, Kabir, Mirabai, Jnaneshwar, Tukaram, Narsi Mehta and Shankardeva composed in the languages of the people, which spread them and made them literary languages as Sanskrit declined.

questions.q: Describe the contribution of Rabindranath Tagore to Bengali literature.
questions.answer: Tagore (1861–1941) wrote novels, dramas, short stories, criticism, music and essays; he won the 1913 Nobel Prize for Geetanjali and influenced all India.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Examine the process of evolution of Northern Indian languages.
questions.answer: Old Apabhramsha took new forms; the Brahmi script of Ashoka became regular by Harsha's time and all northern scripts except Urdu came from it. Hindi grew in forms such as Braj, Avadhi, Maithili and Khadi Boli, with Prithviraj Raso as first book and the Bhakti poets giving devotional literature. Urdu arose after 1192 from Turks and locals and flourished in Deccan and Delhi; Persian was the court language. Punjabi, Bengali, Assamese, Oriya, Gujarati, Marathi, Sindhi and Kashmiri each developed with Bhakti and Sufi saints, missionaries' grammars and presses, and nationalism.

questions.q: Describe the growth of Punjabi and its literature during medieval times.
questions.answer: Punjabi is written in Gurmukhi and Persian scripts. Guru Nanak was the first poet; Sufi saints like Farid used Punjabi, writing in the Persian script; the Adi Granth contains poetry of the gurus and Farid (15th–16th centuries); Guru Gobind Singh composed savaiyyas. Love stories (Heer–Ranjha, Sohni–Mahiwal, Sassi–Punnu) and the story of Puran Bhagat gave early themes; Waris Shah's Heer is a landmark; Bulleh Shah's kafis are sung with fervour.

questions.q: Describe the development of Hindi literature from the Bhakti period to modern times.
questions.answer: Hindi literature began with heroic raso poetry (Prithviraj Raso) and became devotional under the Bhakti movement: Kabir (formless God), Tulsidas (Ramcharit Manas in Avadhi, deifying Rama), Surdas (Sur Sagar in Braj), Mirabai and Raskhan. In the 19th century prose grew with Bharatendu Harishchandra, Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi and Dayanand; later Premchand, Nirala, Jaishankar Prasad, Mahadevi Verma, Pant, Dinkar and Bachchan wrote with a purpose of social reform.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of Christian missionaries and the press to Indian languages and literature.
questions.answer: Missionaries produced dictionaries and grammars (e.g. William Carey's Bengali grammar and dictionary), introduced lithographic presses that published local-language books and journals, and opened schools and colleges teaching local languages. This created an educated class that wanted to read, enriched vocabulary with new words and helped literature, newspapers and nationalism to grow.
